text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming latency > SLO for dedicated-pool:west-1-prd. p95 also elevated. auto-page:oncall-mary. Links: https://internal.metrics/redwood/pool/west-1-prd latency, https://incidents/docs/warmup-playbook

oncall-mary: I'm on it, grabbing metrics + quick triage.
sre-june: saw the spike on the dashboards, streaming tail stalls, clients report chunked streams. p99 ~ 3.8s up from 0.6s.
eng-ryan: are we seeing higher queue depth on the router /pool?
observability-bot: router_queue_depth{pool="west-1-prd"} spiked to 420 (baseline ~30). warmup_pending_instances 0 -> 18 over 90s.
oncall-mary: sounds like autoscaler didn't warm up fast enough. can someone check pool heartbeat / handshake logs?
infra-kat: tailing hotshot logs from pool manager, looks like multiple warmup steps failing handshake with serving runtime:
```
[2026-03-15T22:34:02Z] pool-manager: warmup request sent -> awaiting handshake
[2026-03-15T22:34:12Z] runtime: handshake timeout (err=deadline exceeded)
[2026-03-15T22:34:12Z] pool-manager: retrying warmup (attempt=2)
[2026-03-15T22:34:22Z] runtime: handshake success (attempt=3)
```
infra-kat: warmup attempts succeeded later but were delayed ~20s each, adds up for burst.
sre-june: that aligns with warmup drift hypothesis. any recent changes to heartbeat timeout or handshake window?
eng-ryan: rolled handshake back last week but didn't touch timeouts. however we did change NFS mount retry logic on the warmup image yesterday.
oncall-mary: customer impact? which customers routed to this pool?
support-liam: two enterprise customers (acme-corp, beta-app) reported degraded streaming UX. ticket #INC-1893 created, flagged P2.
pm-alejandra: pushing to standby support channel for customer comms if this continues.
observability-bot: tail latency heatmap attached: hotspots at prefix-KV cold miss and initial streamer setup.
sre-june: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily increase pool target capacity to absorb burst 2) increase handshake timeout to avoid warmup retry storms 3) enable fallback routing to hosted-general pool for new requests 4) throttle non-critical queued requests.
oncall-mary: i'm going to execute manual scale now — will also open a manual warmup window. tagging eng-ryan + infra-kat.
eng-ryan: ack. running scale CLI: `redwoodctl pools scale --id west-1-prd --target 12` (was 6)
infra-kat: applying temporary handshake window: `PATCH /config/pools/west-1-prd` body `{ "handshake_timeout_secs": 40 }`
infra-kat: injecting warmup prefetch to avoid KV coldpath: `redwoodctl warmup --pool west-1-prd --model chat-8k --count 12 --promote`
sre-june: also enabling fallback routing: `featureflag:route_to_hosted_on_capacity=true` (will push only for new cold sessions)
support-liam: drafting customer note: "We're aware of intermittent streaming stalls affecting p99 latency in west-1. We've applied mitigations and are monitoring. No data exposure. We'll update in 30m."
oncall-mary: scale command returned success, target now 12, but warmup queue still backing. looks like instances are passing handshake slowly.
infra-kat: seeing kube node churn in the warmup namespace, some images taking longer due to NFS timeouts mounting model artifacts. investigating registry and NFS latency.
eng-ryan: can we short-circuit heavy NFS coldpull by copying artifacts to local SSD on warmup step? quick patch possible to avoid mount retries.
sre-june: temporary hotfix: increase the artifact mount retry wait and parallelism so mounts happen concurrently rather than serially. infra-kat, can you flip that?
infra-kat: patching warmup init container to `--parallel-mounts=4 --mount-retry=2` now.
observability-bot: within 90s, queue depth down from 420 -> 80, p99 trending down to 1.4s. p95 back near baseline.
oncall-mary: good sign. leaving fallback routing on for extra headroom.
pm-alejandra: good. please capture action items + RCA steps for postmortem. who's owning RCA?
sre-june: I'll own RCA. initial hypothesis: warmup path regression (NFS/mount retries) + conservative handshake timeout causing serial retries and delaying steady-state capacity. need to correlate with deploy yesterday.
eng-ryan: I will revert the NFS mount change from yesterday in the image repo and open PR with improved mount concurrency.
support-liam: sending update to both customers now: "Mitigations applied, latency improving. We will follow up with root cause and timeline."
oncall-mary: live mitigation checklist complete — scaling, handshake timeout bump, warmup prefetch, parallel mounts, fallback routing, rate-limited non-critical traffic.
sre-june: monitoring 30m. if p99 stays <1.5s and queue depth <100 for 30m we can start reverting emergency flags.
infra-kat: NFS team confirms elevated latency during a backup window at 22:30-22:40 UTC. that overlapped our burst. filing cross-team ticket with storage.
pm-alejandra: schedule postmortem for tomorrow 10:00 PT. include oncall-mary, sre-june, eng-ryan, infra-kat, support-liam.
oncall-mary: tagging @here for visibility: incident mitigated, still monitoring. will update thread with final RCA and customer timelines. :white_check_mark:
sre-june: final note for triage log: mitigation steps executed and tracked in runbook https://incidents/docs/warmup-playbook#steps, customer comms logged INC-1893. will add timelines + graphs to PM.
support-liam: customers acknowledged, want SLA credit check later.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (monitoring). duration ~18m. p99 returned to SLO.
oncall-mary: resolving page. good work everyone.
eng-ryan: creating follow-up PR to improve warmup artifact caching and to add a short-circuit fallback when NFS mount latency > 2s.
sre-june: RCA owner assigned. will produce writeup with timelines, root cause, and remediation plan.
support-liam: will update tickets with postmortem link once available.
pm-alejandra: thanks team.
